title: Removing embedded primes from a finite module
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, write $M_{\mathfrak p}$ for localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and define $\operatorname{Supp}(M)=\{\mathfrak p:M_{\mathfrak p}\ne0\}$. An associated prime is a prime equal to $\operatorname{Ann}_R(m)$ for some $m\in M$; an embedded associated prime is an associated prime that is not minimal among the associated primes. Among submodules $K\subseteq M$ whose support is nowhere dense in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ there is a maximal one. For $M'=M/K$, one has $\operatorname{Supp}(M')=\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, $M'$ has no embedded associated primes, and for every $f\in R$ contained in all embedded associated primes of $M$ the localization map gives $M_f\cong M'_f$.

proof.text: By finiteness of the associated-prime set, write Ass(M) as the finite collection of the minimal primes q_j of Supp(M) and the embedded associated primes p_i. Each q_j is associated by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated]. If p=Ann(m) is associated, then m/1 is nonzero in M_p: otherwise some s notin p would satisfy sm=0, forcing s in Ann(m)=p. Thus every associated prime lies in Supp(M).

source.place: Tag 02M6 proof, first paragraph; Tags 00LC and 05BV

proof.text: Define K={m in M | Supp(Rm) is contained in union_i V(p_i)}. Closure under addition follows from Supp(R(m+n)) being contained in Supp(Rm) union Supp(Rn), and scalar closure is immediate. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], K is finite; its support is therefore closed, and it is contained in the finite union union_i V(p_i). Since each p_i is nonminimal in Supp(M), this union contains none of the finitely many generic points q_j of the irreducible components of the Noetherian space Supp(M) (Tag 0052), hence is nowhere dense in Supp(M), so Supp(K) is nowhere dense.

source.place: Tag 02M6 proof, definition of K and the paragraph proving its support is nowhere dense

proof.text: If K' has nowhere-dense support, then K'_{q_j}=0 for every minimal support prime q_j: supports are closed under specialization, so q_j in Supp(K') would put the irreducible component V(q_j) of Supp(M) inside Supp(K'), and V(q_j) minus the other finitely many components is a nonempty open of Supp(M) (Tag 0052). For m in K', (Rm)_{q_j}=0, so q_j is not in Supp(Rm). For any prime r in Supp(Rm), choose a prime r_0 minimal in Supp(Rm) with r_0 subseteq r. The minimal-support theorem applied to the finite module Rm makes r_0 an associated prime of Rm; the submodule theorem puts it in Ass(M), hence r_0 is some q_j or p_i. It cannot be q_j, so r_0=p_i and r lies in V(p_i). Thus m lies in K, proving K' subseteq K and maximality.

Put M'=M/K. Since K_{q_j}=0, M'_{q_j}=M_{q_j}; the closed support of M' therefore contains every minimal q_j of Supp(M), while the quotient map gives Supp(M') subseteq Supp(M), so the two supports are equal. If q=Ann(m-bar) is associated to M', then m is not in K. Hence some prime r in Supp(Rm) lies in no V(p_i); a prime r_0 minimal in Supp(Rm) with r_0 subseteq r is associated to Rm by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated], hence lies in Ass(M) by [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-submodule], and is not any p_i, so r_0 is some q_j and Supp(Rm) contains q_j, and M'_{q_j}=M_{q_j} shows m-bar remains nonzero there, so q subseteq q_j. As q belongs to Supp(M')=Supp(M) and q_j is minimal in that support, q=q_j; thus M' has no embedded associated primes. Finally, if f lies in every p_i, then D(f) misses Supp(K), so K_f=0 and the localization map M_f to M'_f is an isomorphism.
